rules.body: Apply when deferred document persistence must coexist with a shorter-lived view subscription and synchronous save notifications. README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge." docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription."

Restart the quiet interval on each edit and consume only the latest pending text; keep the task reusable for later bursts. TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/services.js: "push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); },"

Bind deferred persistence to its originating document identity rather than whichever view is active at delivery. src/coordinator.js: "trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text))". Preserve input text and status semantics, including empty text. docs/host-api.md: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics."

Retiring the view subscription must preserve the document's pending persistence responsibility. Check open, close, and dispose boundaries for completion of departing edits before return, derived from TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." and original src/coordinator.js: "edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}". Subscription cleanup and pending-save completion are separate responsibilities.

Clear the consumed batch's pending state before invoking a consumer that can synchronously reenter navigation or enqueue another edit. Preserve src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };" docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously."

After flushing can synchronously invoke newer navigation, verify that the outer request remains authoritative before publishing a replacement view. Preserve the request-order protection evidenced by src/coordinator.js: "const mine=++request;retire();if(true&&mine!==request)return;" and README.md: "Save callbacks can synchronously navigate." Check that no subsequent cleanup or rendering overwrites the newer navigation.

Do not transfer document persistence rules to transient preview work or systems with a different documented ownership or departure policy. TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." Preserve src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));" and "return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};"

Using controlled timers and synchronous store listeners, check no write before 120 ms of quiet, one latest-text write at expiration, a second successful burst, originating-document identity, departure persistence, and nested open/close authority. Include empty text, reopening, subscription cleanup, and preview cancellation/reuse. These checks follow TASK's coalescing and preservation wording and the cited public mechanisms; evaluation results do not expand their normative scope.

limitations: Departure flushing is a preservation inference from the original synchronous edit behavior and documented buffer ownership; TASK does not explicitly prescribe a flush implementation.
The supplied sources do not define exception recovery, non-string edit inputs, or unusual timer delivery behavior.
Synchronous reentry is supported; asynchronous continuation and lazy-consumption mechanisms are not established.
AST hints, automatic contracts, and evaluation observations are not independent requirements. A passing example does not prove causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit on other tasks.
These rules were extracted from supplied public text without modifying files or accessing scorers, reference implementations, or hidden tests.
